title: Cartesian affinization square for an open inside a quasi-affine scheme
statement: Let $u:U\hookrightarrow V$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], where both $U$ and $V$ are quasi-affine, meaning isomorphic to quasi-compact open subschemes of affine schemes. Put $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ and $B=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, let $r:B\to A$ be restriction, and let $j_U:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $j_V:V\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ be the canonical morphisms corresponding to the identity on sections [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The square with top arrow $j_U$, left arrow $\mathrm{id}_U$, right arrow $\operatorname{Spec}r$, and bottom arrow $j_V\circ u:U\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. Equivalently, the inverse-image open subscheme $(\operatorname{Spec}r)^{-1}(j_V(u(U)))$ is $j_U(U)$, and its morphism to the open subscheme $j_V(u(U))$ is identified with the identity of $U$ by $j_U$ and $j_V\circ u$.
